description.text: Advanced Energy provides highly engineered, critical, precision power conversion, measurement, and control solutions to our global customers. We design, manufacture, sell and service precision power products that transform, refine, and modify the raw electrical power coming from either the utility or the building facility and convert it into various types of highly controllable, usable power that is predictable, repeatable, and customizable to meet the necessary requirements for powering a wide range of complex equipment. Our products enable customers to reduce or optimize their energy consumption through increased power conversion efficiency, power density, power coupling, and process control across a wide range of applications. We are organized on a global, functional basis and operate as a single segment of power electronics conversion products. Within this segment, our products are sold in the Semiconductor Equipment, Data Center Computing, Industrial and Medical, and Telecom and Networking markets. We incorporated in Colorado in 1981 and reincorporated in Delaware in 1995. Our executive offices are located at 1595 Wynkoop Street, Suite 800, Denver, Colorado 80202, and our telephone number is 970-407-6555.

about.description_short: Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement, and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE's power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing, and healthcare. With engineering know-how and responsive worldwide service and support, the company builds collaborative partnerships to meet evolving technology requirements, drive customer growth, and innovate the future of power.

analysis_md:
# AEIS — Advanced Energy Industries, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. Price $238.05 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap (est) $9.189B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Precision power conversion, measurement and control: plasma/RF power for semiconductor wafer-fab equipment (eVerest, eVoS platforms), rack power for hyperscaler data centers, plus industrial and medical power. Q2 2026 (search results): revenue $574.1M, +30% YoY; Semiconductor Equipment a record $278.3M (+32.8% YoY); Data Center Computing $191.5M (+35.2% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $2.74. Management guided H2 2026 semiconductor revenue up ~50% YoY, full-year data-center revenue growth of at least 50%, Q4 gross margin in the 42% range, and 2026 capex of $180–195M (raised, to support growth). Capacity is being added in Malaysia, the Philippines and Mexico, plus a new 500,000 sq ft Thailand facility (initial production late 2026 / early 2027) that lifts revenue capacity from ~$2.5B toward ~$3.5B once built out.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $233,300,000; capex $107,400,000; SBC $55,700,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $70,200,000 = $1.82/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $1.82).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $709,980,000 for FY2025 per financials_history.csv — **not credible as a run rate**: it is inflated by a −$561,400,000 ΔNWC swing in the filed history (a balance-sheet release, not recurring cash earnings). The conservative OCF-based series is the base used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but violently cyclical: OE/share $2.49 (FY2021), $2.78 (FY2022), $3.09 (FY2023), $0.74 (FY2024), $1.82 (FY2025) — revenue fell −10.3% in FY2023 and −10.5% in FY2024 in the semi downturn, then +21.38% in FY2025 (latest rev YoY, key_numbers.md).
- Balance sheet: net debt −$223.7M (net cash; cash $791,200,000 vs total debt $567,500,000, financials_history.csv), lease liabilities $111,500,000 (dcf_numbers.json). Shares diluted (latest): 38,600,000; share count CAGR +0.77% (mild dilution, no buyback tailwind).

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, run for STALE_FY — quoted in full, not used as the base):**
- OCF: FY $233,300,000 − prior YTD $74,100,000 + current YTD $79,000,000 = **TTM $238,200,000**
- Capex: FY $107,400,000 − prior YTD $42,000,000 + current YTD $86,100,000 = **TTM $151,500,000**
- SBC: FY $55,700,000 − prior YTD $26,600,000 + current YTD $39,500,000 = **TTM $68,600,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **42,300,000**
- **TTM OE total $18,100,000 → TTM OE/share $0.43**

**Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): $1.82/share** (key_numbers.md; the last-3 median and the latest FY coincide at $1.82). The TTM figure was *not* adopted: TTM capex of $151,500,000 is growth capex for the capacity build (2026 guided capex $180–195M, vs TTM D&A of $62,600,000 in fundamentals.json), and the conservative definition charges every dollar of it against OE as if it were maintenance. The median base already spans a trough year (FY2024, $0.74) and an already capex-elevated FY2025 ($107,400,000), so it is the least-distorted base; the TTM $0.43 is disclosed as bear-side evidence. The verdict is identical on either base — Tier D, IRR at the floor (see method range).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: real qualification switching costs in plasma power for leading-edge fabs (eVerest/eVoS design wins validated on yield/throughput) and in hyperscaler rack power, against through-cycle ROIC that collapsed in the trough and gross margin well below the level of a decade ago. Evidence (fundamentals.json): roic_proxy 19.1% (FY2021), 19.9% (FY2022), 8.8% (FY2023), 2.8% (FY2024), 13.1% (FY2025); gross margin 36.6% / 36.6% / 35.8% / 35.7% / 37.7% over FY2021–25, 39.3% TTM — recovering, with the ~42% Q4 level guided rather than delivered, and structurally below the 50%+ earned in 2016–18 after the mix shift toward data-center power and acquisitions. That record — above the cost of capital in upcycles, below it in troughs — supports a 5, not a 7+.
- FOR: leading plasma power position (eVerest/eVoS) with customer-validated yield/throughput gains at leading-edge logic and memory nodes — high qualification switching costs in fab tools; design wins in hyperscaler data-center rack power incl. next-generation and 800V programs, plus second-wave customers ramping 2027; broad precision-power portfolio across semiconductor, data center, industrial and medical with global engineering and manufacturing scale; net cash balance sheet (net debt −$223.7M) funds the capacity build without leverage.
- AGAINST: through-cycle ROIC mediocre and volatile (19.9% FY2022 → 2.8% FY2024 → 13.1% FY2025); gross margin 35.7–37.7% over the last five fiscal years, structurally below 2016–18's 50%+; deep cyclicality (revenue −10% in both FY2023 and FY2024, OE/share $3.09 → $0.74); customer/end-market concentration — semi capex and a handful of hyperscalers set demand, competition (e.g. MKS) is program-by-program; growth now requires heavy capex ($180–195M guided for 2026 vs ~$62M D&A), so OE lags reported earnings through the build.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (engine 5.4.0, 2026-10-18)
**Growth recalibration (written reason):** the engine's blended growth start is 1.26% (key_numbers.md), built from rev CAGR 5y 4.91%, rev CAGR 3y −0.85%, latest rev YoY 21.38% and OE/share CAGR 2y −23.30%. The 3-yr CAGR and OE CAGR are trough artifacts of the 2023–24 semi downturn; against actual recent prints — FY2025 revenue +21.38%, TTM revenue +24.6% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 +30% YoY, H2 semiconductor guided up ~50% YoY and data-center FY growth guided to at least 50% — a 1.26% base start is below what the company just printed with no written justification available for it. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated upward via offsets (−0.0626 / +0.0374 / +0.1374 / +0.2374 / +0.3374 vs g_base) to −5 / +5 / **+15** / +25 / +35%: the base start (15%) still sits below the current +25–30% prints, reflecting semi cyclicality and the guided nature of the H2 ramp; the super-bull start (35%) sits above the latest quarterly print only on the strength of the ~50% H2/data-center guidance. Probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 (bear weight widened per OE_VOLATILE); OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults). Price $238.05.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −5.0% | 0.75 | Semi cycle turns down again as in 2023–24; hyperscaler digestion | $8.17 | 2.88% |
| Bear | 30% | 5.0% | 0.90 | Upcycle fades fast; capex stays high into softening demand | $14.89 | 3.31% |
| Base | 30% | 15.0% | 1.00 | Strong 2026–27 on semi/DC ramps, then normal cyclical fade over the CAP | $24.96 | 4.00% |
| Bull | 15% | 25.0% | 1.10 | Current print pace sustains; Thailand ramps on time; margin reaches guided ~42% | $41.06 | 5.11% |
| Super bull | 10% | 35.0% | 1.25 | Guided ~50% H2/DC growth sustains for years; share gains compound | $69.05 | 6.92% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $26.25 (−89.0% vs price), IV@12% $35.91, IV@10% $46.82, weighted IRR 4.13%, base-case IRR 4.00%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D → bull D; scenario range 2.88%–6.92%). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 0.76%, terminal value 21.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 8.45x, net debt −3.19x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- **Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $26.25 · 20% at $17.73 · 25% at $13.16.**

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full inputs are quoted above. The TTM base ($0.43/share) was *not* adopted — it charges the guided growth-capex build ($151,500,000 TTM capex; $180–195M guided for 2026, vs $62,600,000 TTM D&A) entirely against OE. The median-of-3 base ($1.82) is used, with the TTM figure disclosed as bear-side evidence; the TTM revenue strength (+24.6% YoY) is instead reflected in the recalibrated scenario growth starts.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real cyclicality, not an artifact — OE/share $3.09 (FY2023) → $0.74 (FY2024) → $1.82 (FY2025) across the semi downturn. Handled with the normalized median base and bear-side weighting (super bear + bear = 45%).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024): explained by non-cash addbacks in a trough-earnings year, not a one-off item — FY2024 net income $54,214,000 vs OCF $130,800,000 (financials_history.csv), with D&A $68,500,000 and SBC $45,900,000 added back in OCF while operating margin compressed to 2.5% (fundamentals.json). Tax was a small benefit (−$3,900,000), not a deposit swing. ## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is robustness, not a point estimate: every defensible method lands in Tier D. The preliminary engine run (blend growth 1.26%, default probabilities) gave weighted IRR 3.31% and IV@15% $15.20 (dcf_numbers.json, preliminary run). The TTM base ($0.43/share) would print lower still. This final run deliberately recalibrates growth *up* to starts anchored on the current +25–30% prints and the ~50% H2/data-center guidance — and still produces IV@15% of $26.25 against a $238.05 price. The gap is not a growth-assumption dispute; it is that the price capitalizes non-GAAP earnings power (~$11/share annualized at the Q2 print, per search results) while owner's earnings — after SBC ($68,600,000 TTM) and the capex the growth requires ($151,500,000 TTM, $180–195M guided) — are $0.43 TTM and $1.82 on the normalized base.
- Quality is real but cyclical: record semiconductor revenue, validated plasma platforms, hyperscaler design wins, net cash. None of that is in dispute. What is in dispute is paying ~131x normalized OE/share (price $238.05 vs base $1.82, both from key_numbers.md) for a business whose revenue fell 10% in each of the last two down years and whose ROIC fell to 2.8% in the trough.
- Risks to this verdict (i.e. what would make it wrong): the data-center power business becoming a durable, less cyclical franchise (800V/second-wave ramps in 2027–28) at structurally higher margins, converting today's growth capex into OE at high incremental returns — the super-bull case gestures at this and still reaches only $69.05 at a 15% discount rate. A buyer at $238.05 needs substantially more than the super-bull case as modeled.
